{
  "need": "Status",
  "secondary": { "name": "Belonging" },
  "read": "A blowout win is the worst moment to address selfishness because the scoreboard is telling every kid they were right. Each one is riding a status high — points scored, highlight plays — and they need that feeling to matter. The belonging angle is real too: selfish play often spreads like a contagion when peers model it and nobody calls it out, so fitting in with the 'scorers' became the norm tonight.",
  "pull": { "collapse": "Enforcer", "instinct": "You want to walk into that locker room and rip them — 'You won ugly and I'm not celebrating that' — but public shaming after a win feels like you're stealing something from them, so they stop trusting your feedback and start playing to prove you wrong instead of playing for each other." },
  "mentorMove": "Acknowledge the win genuinely and briefly, then name the gap between what they showed and what they're capable of — framing the selfish play not as a character flaw but as a missed opportunity to be an elite unit. Hold the standard for team-first ball while crediting their talent.",
  "holdFirm": [
    "The standard is ball movement, reads, and helping each other look good — every game, every score.",
    "Tonight does not get counted as a template for how this team plays."
  ],
  "stayFlexible": [
    "Let them name what they saw on the floor — give them the chance to self-diagnose before you diagnose them.",
    "Welcome their ideas on how the team tracks unselfishness in practice this week — assists, screens, whatever they own."
  ],
  "forceLevel": { "level": 3, "label": "Collaboration" },
  "script": [
    { "phase": "Connection", "words": "Bring it in. W is a W, and I'm not taking that from you — you competed and you finished. Give yourselves a breath." },
    { "phase": "Curiosity", "words": "Now I want to hear from you honestly — when you watch film on tonight, what does the ball look like moving? Not the score. The ball." },
    { "phase": "Collaboration", "words": "Here's what I saw: a bunch of talented players playing like strangers instead of a team. The scary part? We won anyway. That means we haven't even touched our ceiling yet. But if we keep playing that way, we will hit a ceiling — because the next team that's also talented will be connected, and we won't be. So tell me: what does connected look like for us this week in practice? What do we want to measure?" },
    { "phase": "Commitment", "words": "I'm not letting tonight's style slide — that's not who we're building here. And I'm pushing on this because I have high standards for this group and I genuinely believe you can play at a level most teams never reach. That version of us doesn't exist yet, and I want to build it with you. We good?" }
  ],
  "longGame": "Winning ugly is a slow poison — it rewards individual habits and quietly erodes trust. Over the next few weeks, build public rituals around assists and screens: call them out loudly in practice, put them on the whiteboard, make unselfishness visible and high-status so the players who give up shots for a teammate become the ones the group looks up to."
}
situation: My team won big and played selfish, ugly ball the entire game.
